chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Suleyman ibn Sama'ah, from Dawood al-Hazza', from Abdul Malik ibn Bahr, the companion of Al-Lu'lu', who said:

Whoever intends to wear a sandal and a yellowish one (gradually turning to white) falls to him, he will not be deprived of wealth and children; and whoever falls to him a black one, he will not be deprived of grief and anxiety.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the color of sandals in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from the school of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the Shia concept of *isharah* (spiritual indication) where physical attributes reflect inner or future states. While often interpreted as omens, scholars note it serves as a reminder to maintain spiritual mindfulness in daily actions, linking the color yellow (often associated with vitality or gold) to material and familial blessings, and black to emotional heaviness. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on finding divine signs in the mundane aspects of life.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Suleyman Bin Sama’at, from Dawood Al Haza’a, from Abdul Malik Bin Bahr, a companions of Al Lului who said,

‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘The one who intends wearing the sandals, so he takes to yellow going on towards whiteness, would not be reduced to poverty, nor be without children, and the one who goes for the black, would not be short of grief and stress’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Sulayman ibn Sama‘ah from Dawud al-Hadhdha’ from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Bahr Sahib al-Lu’Lu who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one wants to wear shoes and he finds yellow toward whiteness shoes, he will not live without property or children; but if one finds black shoes he will not live without sadness and anxieties.’”
